lines: Good tools held. So did I. I will inspect both before sleeping.
My grip held when it had to. I will think about that for a while.
The handle held, the edge held, and I held on behind them.
I will inspect every tool I carried. I may inspect my knees too.
A good grip saved me more than once tonight.
I made it back with work to do and hands still able to do it.
Nothing tests a tool like <dark_gray><wavy>fear</wavy></dark_gray>. Nothing tests a person faster.
I know what strain does to metal. Now I know what it does to me.
I did not feel brave. I just kept moving.
The bell stopped ringing, but I still hear it.
My hammer came back chipped. I came back shaking.
I lost my footing once and thought that was the end.
The shield beside me broke before my handle did.
I remember every swing that came too close.
There is blood on my apron that is not mine.
I kept counting breaths until the fighting stopped.
My arms are sore, my ears are ringing, and I am alive.
I dropped one tool and had no chance to pick it up.
Someone pulled me behind a wall when my legs gave out.
I need water, quiet, and a long look at everything that kept me alive.
